rules: New independent experiment; do not restore deleted experiment directories or reuse their artifacts.
Original Pattern labels from pattern.datasets: 11 signed binary inputs, presence of a four-bit substring, 8 ReLU hidden units.
Shared head: four task-specific codebook entries, one shared hidden bias, one shared readout and one output bias. C[0] is fixed to zero.
Search receives only source support/query observations and the number of categories. No true connections, window positions, active-edge count, per-column degree or code capacities.

One shared alpha for all ten discovery tasks, four independent ongoing numeric initializations per task. Each numeric Adam step freezes alpha; each architecture Adam step uses query labels and freezes numeric values, or differentiates through one virtual Adam step in the unrolled control.

All configurations and restarts have independent optimizer moments. Gradients for each numeric fit are not averaged over unrelated fits; architecture objectives average over tasks and numeric replicas.

Pilot tunes two numeric rates, three architecture rates and two schedules, two search seeds each. Annealed schedule lowers temperature and adds late entropy minimization; the soft control keeps temperature one and no entropy penalty.
Canonicalize hard indexators only by renaming nonzero groups and permuting hidden columns. Never use teacher alignment before numeric fitting.

Rank architecture checkpoints and numeric fitting settings by mean selection BCE across both selection functions and all fresh starts, after each start's checkpoint is selected by query BCE. Never rank by inherited soft-network quality or structural agreement with oracle.

Confirm the two best pilot configurations using three new search seeds, first-order and differentiable one-step controls. Confirmation uses the selected fixed numerical fitting settings. Rank configuration/order by the mean of three seeds after each seed's checkpoint selection; primary seed is chosen on selection BCE within the winning group.

Freeze selected architecture and numerical settings before constructing target labels. Four target function types were studied historically; this is a new split/seed replication, not a new benchmark family.
Final evaluation uses fixed structures and fresh numerical initializations, equal restart/step budgets, query-only checkpoint and start selection, disjoint test observations.

Controls: learned sharing, learned support without tying, random sharing on that support, shuffled indexator with the same code counts, initial random indexator, dense shared head, ordinary dense MLP, and privileged true indexator.
Report actual support/query loss and recall curves, entropy, inherited soft/hard gap, fresh-refit quality and selected indexator heatmaps. No software tests, commits or publication.
